initial_presentation: The patient is a 78-year-old right-handed female with a history of hyperlipidemia and previous smoking. She presented with dysarthria and progressive muscle weakness, which began 10 years ago. Initially, the weakness affected her lower extremities, more pronounced on the right side, and gradually led to falls and the need for a rolling walker. Over the next two years, the weakness extended to her bilateral upper extremities. She also reported muscle stiffness in the lower extremities, along with progressive dysphagia and dysarthria over the past few years. Currently, she uses a wheelchair for mobility. She denied sensory abnormalities, fluctuations in weakness, neck or back pain, shooting pain, bowel or bladder incontinence, muscle twitching, muscle pain, urine discoloration, double vision, or breathing difficulty. On examination, she had impaired shoulder shrugging bilaterally, indicating spinal accessory nerve involvement. Using the Muscle Research Grading System (MRGS), her strength was graded as 4 in bilateral upper and lower extremities proximally, 4+ distally in bilateral upper extremities, and 4- in bilateral lower extremities. Spasticity was noted in both upper and lower extremities. Deep tendon reflexes were exaggerated in the bilateral patellar, biceps, and triceps regions. Sustained ankle clonus was present bilaterally. The plantar reflex was mute, and Hoffman’s sign was positive bilaterally. Sensory and cerebellar system examinations were unremarkable.
A 46-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of cough, fever, generalized muscle aches, sore throat, progressively worsening shortness of breath, and night sweats.

A 14-year-old female presented with progressive deformity in valgus of the lower limbs and muscle hypotrophy. Symptoms began at 15 months old, including gait instability, reduced range of motion in hands and arms, and impaired gross and fine motor skills. She is the second child of healthy consanguineous parents, with a mother who had three pregnancies and three births. The pregnancy was uneventful, with a vaginal delivery at 39 weeks, a birth weight of 2,600 g (5th centile), and a birth length of 45 cm (25th centile). Developmental milestones were normal, with sitting at 6 months and walking at 15 months. She has normal intelligence and good academic performance. On general examination, she appeared healthy but was wheelchair-bound. Her weight was 25 kg (3rd centile), height 132 cm (below 3rd centile), and head circumference 52 cm (16th centile). Physical examination revealed diminished sensitivity in hands, forearms, feet, and calves, scoliosis, and pes cavus. Muscle atrophy was noted, especially in the forearms and calves, with finger contractures. No dysmorphic features, vocal paresis, or breathing difficulties were observed. Reflexes were diminished in the Achilles and biceps. Muscle strength was 4/5 in hands, forearms, and shoulder girdle, and 3/5 in thighs, calves, and feet (MRC scale). Cranial nerves were intact, and no dysautonomic signs were present.

A 10-month-old girl was brought to the endocrine unit due to significant and rapid weight gain. She was delivered at full term via normal vaginal delivery, weighing 3.0 kg at birth. She is the second child of healthy parents who are not obese, with third-degree consanguinity. There was no history of gestational diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, or excessive maternal weight gain during pregnancy. Increased appetite was observed at around two months of age, with feeding demands every half to one hour. Her weight increased to 9.5 kg at four months and 15 kg at six months. There were no reports of lethargy, dry skin, constipation, excessive hair growth, seizures, or visual or sleep disturbances. A paternal uncle and a male cousin had a history of early onset obesity. Physical examination showed generalized body fat distribution, a rounded face, and deep skinfolds, with acanthosis nigricans in the axillae and neck folds. Vital signs were normal. Her weight was 19 kg, length 71.0 cm, and body mass index 37.7 kg/m2. Anthropometric measurements were calculated using WHO Anthroplus software. Ophthalmological evaluation was normal. Systemic examination was unremarkable.

A 20-year-old male from Brazil presented with low back pain persisting for 8 months, without any associated trauma.

At the initial consultation, the patient was a 25-year-old first-time pregnant woman at 22 weeks and 4 days of gestation. The pregnancy had been mostly uneventful except for findings on antenatal anatomy scans. Ultrasounds showed a fetus with both kidneys enlarged and echogenic, multiple cysts within the kidney tissue, absence of amniotic fluid, and a non-visible bladder. Prenatal screening for Trisomy 21 and Trisomy 18 was negative. A three-generation family history was taken, revealing German and Scottish ancestry for the patient and Irish and English ancestry for her partner, with no known consanguinity or congenital anomalies. Due to the poor prognosis for the fetus, labor was induced for therapeutic termination of pregnancy. A male stillborn fetus was delivered at 22 weeks and 5 days of gestation. External examination and autopsy were conducted. The fetus exhibited facial features consistent with Potter sequence, a high-arched palate, and maxillary hypoplasia, with no orofacial clefting. Severe elbow contractures and bilateral elbow pterygia were noted. The left hand had post-axial polydactyly (six digits) and full cutaneous syndactyly between the second and third, and fourth and fifth digits. The right hand had partial syndactyly between the third and fourth digits. No polydactyly or syndactyly was observed in the toes. Bilateral clubfeet could not be excluded, considering positional changes. The skin examination was consistent with the gestational age and otherwise unremarkable. Autopsy confirmed pulmonary hypoplasia and bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multicystic renal cortical dysplasia. The right kidney weighed 8 g, and the left weighed 5 g, with a combined weight of 13 g (age-related norm: 4.77 ± 1.39 g). The cysts were disorganized, varied in shape and size, and up to 0.5 cm in diameter, lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with collars of smooth muscle. The ureters and bladder were identified without obvious abnormalities. The testes were intra-abdominal and consistent with the gestational age. A skeletal survey showed no obvious skeletal congenital anomalies beyond the post-axial polydactyly of the left hand.

A 10-month-old female presented with recurrent infections in the maxillofacial region, characterized by swelling or abscess formation in the left cheek and purulent discharge from a preauricular pit over a period of 4 months. Physical examination revealed a swollen, erythematous lesion on the left cheek. Additionally, a pit with white purulent secretions was noted in the intertragic notch, along with a small cutaneous dimple in the left parotid gland area. Examination of the external auditory canal showed no fistula track, and other head and neck examinations were normal.

A 52-year-old woman reported a progressive decline in vision in both eyes over the past two to three years. There is no family history of eye diseases, including her deceased parents. Her best-corrected visual acuities were 20/63 in the right eye and 20/50 in the left eye.
